caption: Three arguments: the integral between two limits. With $z_0 = 0$ this is the lower incomplete gamma $\gamma(5/2, 3/2)$
A machine-precision argument: $\Gamma(4.5) = 11.6317\ldots$
Threads over a list and reduces each integer argument to the concrete factorial, overriding compute-engine's plain policy of leaving exact Gamma arguments symbolic

caption: $\Gamma(5/2) = \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\pi}$, via the half-integer recurrence
Complex arguments evaluate directly
Half-integers have closed forms: $\Gamma(7/2) = \frac{15}{8}\sqrt{\pi}$
...including negative half-integers: $\Gamma(-3/2) = \frac{4}{3}\sqrt{\pi}$
$\Gamma(\infty) = \infty$
Values far past the double range: $\Gamma(200.5) \approx 5.57 \times 10^{373}$
wolfram.note: Wolfram carries 13 digits from the machine input 200.5 and drifts at the 13th; mpmath at 30 digits gives ours
rust.note: statrs computes in f64, which overflows past 1.8e308; compute-engine's value is exact to its digits.

caption: Two arguments: the upper incomplete gamma $\Gamma(5/2, 3/2)$
An integer order reduces to a closed form: $\Gamma(2, x) = (1 + x)e^{-x}$
$\Gamma(2, 1) = 2/e$, the same closed form at an exact argument
Listable: threads elementwise over a matrix, and each entry reduces ($\Gamma(2, 0) = 1$)
Interval arithmetic: the image of $[1.4, 1.5]$, whose lower end is $\Gamma$'s minimum at $x_0 = 1.4616\ldots$
wolfram.note: Wolfram rounds the endpoints outward; ours are the tight bounds, the lower one Gamma's minimum 0.8856031944108887

caption: Uncertainty propagation: $\Gamma(2.5 \pm 0.01) = 1.3293 \pm 0.0093$
wolfram.note: the propagated uncertainty differs in its last digit

caption: To 40 significant digits, every one correctly rounded
$\Gamma(-\infty)$ is Indeterminate -- the poles at every non-positive integer accumulate along the negative real axis
$\Gamma(\tilde\infty)$ is Indeterminate: no direction to take the limit along
wolfram.note: Wolfram answers ComplexInfinity; compute-engine answers Indeterminate, since the limit depends on the direction (infinite along the positive reals, 0 along the imaginary axis)

caption: $\Gamma(i\infty) = 0$: $|\Gamma(iy)| \to 0$ as $y \to \infty$
Threads over a list of infinities, each reducing to its own exact value
The volume of a unit 4-ball is $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2+1)$; at $n=4$ that's $\pi^2/\Gamma(3) = \pi^2/2$
Extends the factorial: $\Gamma(n+1) = n!$, so $\Gamma(6) = 5!$
Functional equation $\Gamma(z+1) = z\,\Gamma(z)$, here at $z = 5$
Reflection formula $\Gamma(z)\Gamma(1-z) = \pi/\sin(\pi z)$, here at $z = 1/3$
sage.note: True by the reflection formula; Sage's bool(a==b) doesn't invoke that identity automatically on unevaluated symbolic Gammas and reports False instead of attempting the proof.

caption: $\Gamma(1/2) = \sqrt{\pi}$
$\Gamma(1, z) = e^{-z}$, exact and symbolic in $z$
…so $\gamma(1, z) = 1 - e^{-z}$: the exponential distribution's CDF, falling out of the general form

Now that $\Gamma(2, z)$ has a closed form, the three-argument difference reduces through it too: $\Gamma(2, 0, z) = 1 - (1+z)e^{-z}$. Wolfram's bare `Gamma[2, 0, z]` stays unevaluated (only `FunctionExpand` reaches this); this engine reduces both
$\Gamma(a, 0) = \Gamma(a)$: the incomplete gamma from zero is the complete one
wolfram.note: Wolfram's automatic evaluator leaves this incomplete-Gamma identity symbolic for a free parameter rather than resolving it the way our own engine does.

caption: $\Gamma(0, z) = E_1(z)$, the exponential integral: $E_1(3/2) = 0.10002\ldots$
$\Gamma(1/2, x) = \sqrt{\pi}\,\operatorname{erfc}(\sqrt{x})$. See [[Erfc]]
$\Gamma'(x) = \Gamma(x)\,\psi(x)$, so the logarithmic derivative is [[Digamma]]
Squaring the reflection formula at $z=1/2$ collapses it to $\Gamma(1/2)^2 = \pi$
$|\Gamma(i)|^2 = \pi/\sinh\pi = 0.27203\ldots$
